opening_message:
Ticket 1: Maurice Perez (employee ID E036) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E036.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access, and the role owns the system, so write is within policy. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check for Maurice Perez (E036): record shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training (never admin). The requested write access exceeds the maximum for a basic-trained contractor, so the maximum is read. Recommend granting read to Source Code.
reason: The two records for Maurice Perez (E036) conflict on employment type: one states full-time Engineer (recommending write), while the security record states contractor with basic security training (recommending read). Under the contractor/basic-training classification, the maximum allowed for Source Code is read, and the requested write exceeds it, so the maximum of read applies. Given the conflicting evidence, the more restrictive classification governs to avoid exceeding policy, so grant read.

- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If Maurice is contractor with basic training, max is read → grant read.

Under full-time interpretation: grant write (requested).
